name: Microsoft Outlook (Graph)
summary: Registering the app takes minutes. Trust is the gate: without publisher verification, users in other tenants often can't consent, and many orgs require an admin to approve mail scopes regardless.

composio.note: Composio-managed works. Org tenants may still show “Needs admin approval”, which is a tenant policy and not something Composio controls.

capabilities.label: Sign in (work & personal accounts)
capabilities.why: Basic sign-in and profile are exempt from the unverified-publisher consent block

capabilities.label: Read mail & calendar
capabilities.why: Users outside your tenant can't consent to an unverified multitenant app. Admins may also require approval

capabilities.label: Org-wide access with no user present
capabilities.why: Application permissions always need tenant admin consent

gates.label: Publisher verification
gates.plain: Microsoft confirms your company is real before other organisations' users can consent.

skip.reason: Users in your own tenant aren't blocked by the unverified-publisher rule

gates.label: Tenant admin consent
gates.plain: Each customer's IT admin has to approve org-wide access.

steps.title: Use a work (Entra) account, not a personal one
steps.detail: Apps registered under a personal Microsoft account can't be publisher-verified.
steps.human: Create or choose an Entra tenant for your company

steps.title: Register a multitenant app
steps.detail: Entra admin center → App registrations → New. Supported account types: any org directory (+ personal accounts if needed). Add the redirect URI (Composio BYO: https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback).
steps.agent: Fill in the registration and add delegated Graph permissions
steps.human: Create it while signed in; store the client secret

steps.title: Verify your publisher domain (DNS)
steps.detail: Add a DNS-verified custom domain to the tenant or set the publisher domain. You need it before you can verify as a publisher.
steps.agent: Generate the DNS TXT record and check propagation
steps.human: Add the record at your DNS provider

steps.title: Enroll in the Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program
steps.detail: Partner Center creates a Partner One ID (formerly MPN ID) and verifies your business: legal entity, address and an email on your domain.
steps.agent: Pre-fill the enrollment details; track verification email
steps.human: Provide legal entity details and approve the verification email

steps.title: Mark the app as publisher verified
steps.detail: App registration → Branding & properties → Add Partner ID. The user needs the right roles in both Entra and Partner Center.
steps.human: Enter the Partner One ID and click Verify

steps.title: Get tenant admin consent where required
steps.detail: Application permissions, and tenants that block user consent, need an admin to grant consent through the admin-consent URL.
steps.agent: Generate the admin-consent URL and a one-page explainer for IT
steps.human: Send it to the customer's admin

alternatives.label: Use delegated Mail.Read (acts as the signed-in user) instead of application permissions
alternatives.tradeoff: The agent only sees mailboxes of users who connected, not the whole org.

facts.claim: Users in other tenants can't consent to unverified multitenant apps asking for more than sign-in
facts.title: Microsoft Learn: Publisher verification overview
facts.quote: Note Beginning November 2020, if risk-based step-up consent is enabled, users can't consent to most newly registered multitenant apps that aren't publisher verified.

facts.claim: The block applies only to users in tenants other than the one where the app is registered
facts.title: Microsoft Learn: Publisher verification overview
facts.quote: The policy applies to apps that were registered after November 8, 2020, which use OAuth 2.0 to request permissions that extend beyond the basic sign-in and read user profile, and which request consent from users in tenants that aren't the tenant where the app is registered.

facts.claim: Publisher verification needs a verified Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program account
facts.title: Microsoft Learn: Publisher verification overview
facts.quote: Verifying an app includes using a Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program (CPP), formerly known as Microsoft Partner Network (MPN), account that's been verified and associating the verified PartnerID with an app registration.

facts.claim: You verify by entering your Partner One ID on the app registration
facts.title: Microsoft Learn: Mark an app as publisher verified
facts.quote: Enter your Partner One ID and select Verify and save .

facts.claim: Application permissions need tenant-wide admin consent
facts.title: Microsoft Learn: Grant tenant-wide admin consent
facts.quote: Cloud Application Administrator, AI Administrator, or Application Administrator, for granting consent for apps requesting any permission for any API, except Microsoft Graph app roles (application permissions).

launchToday: Composio-managed Outlook works today for many consumer and business accounts.
Start Partner Program enrollment now: business verification is the long pole and runs in parallel with your build.
Ship sign-in plus User.Read first. Those scopes are exempt from the unverified-publisher block.
rejections: Publisher verification fails: the Partner One ID is a location ID, not the CPP account ID
The signed-in user lacks roles in Entra or Partner Center
App registered under a personal Microsoft account

blockers.problem: “Need admin approval” on the consent screen
blockers.fix: The tenant blocks user consent or the app is unverified. Finish publisher verification and send the customer's admin your admin-consent URL.
Multitenant apps registered after Nov 2020 that request more than basic scopes need a verified publisher before users in other tenants can consent.

uncertain: Microsoft doesn't publish how long Partner Center business verification takes. The 1–10 day range is our estimate.
Whether a given customer tenant needs admin consent depends on that tenant's own policy.
